source_text: Ignis perpetuus et memoriale coram Domino. Noli extinguere Spiritum. Amen.
thought_title: Perpetual fire and remembrance before the Lord
orientation: Origen is concluding his homily on the lamp and the bread of the Presence, applying the perpetual fire of the sanctuary to the Spirit within the believer.
pass_a_gloss: Perpetual fire and remembrance before the Lord. Do not extinguish the Spirit. Amen.

choices.why: The source phrase names the sanctuary fire that was to burn continually; rendering it literally preserves the ritual reference.
The phrase echoes Leviticus 24:7 where the frankincense is placed on the bread as a memorial before the Lord; literal rendering keeps the cultic sense.
This is a direct echo of 1 Thessalonians 5:19; the imperative force of 'noli' with the infinitive is preserved as a prohibition.
rejected: You must not put out the Spirit

pass_b_english: A perpetual fire and a remembrance before the Lord (Leviticus 6:12-13). Do not extinguish the Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19). Amen.

problems.source_quote: Ignis perpetuus et memoriale coram Domino
problems.why: Leviticus 24:7 is about showbread and frankincense, not perpetual fire. This refers to Leviticus 6:12-13 (LXX/Vulgate numbering) about the perpetual fire on the altar.
problems.ruling: Leviticus 24:7 covers frankincense/showbread, not 'ignis perpetuus'; perpetual fire is Lev 6:12-13.

fixed: Corrected scripture reference from Leviticus 24:7 to Leviticus 6:12-13, which is the passage about the perpetual fire on the altar.
